name: keltner_channel_trend_5s
author: adapted from quant_system
thesis: Keltner Channels use ATR-based envelopes which adapt to volatility better than standard deviation-based Bollinger Bands. When price sustains outside the Keltner Channel, it signals a strong trend that ATR-normalized volatility can't explain — i.e., genuine directional force. The inefficiency exists because most retail traders don't use Keltner Channels, preferring Bollinger Bands, so the crowd isn't positioned for KC-based signals.
mechanism: Keltner channels use ATR-based envelopes to identify when price has moved beyond its normal volatility range. Excursions beyond the channel indicate a liquidity-driven overshoot. Market makers and mean-reversion algorithms enter opposing positions at the extremes, pulling price back within the channel as the impulsive flow is absorbed.

exit.signal_exit: exit if close re-enters inside channel for 3 bars

weaknesses: 38% win rate means 5-8 loss streaks are normal. Capital allocation must account for extended drawdowns.
In rangebound markets (60%+ of days), Keltner signals whipsaw repeatedly. ADX filter helps but lags.
ATR-based channels adapt slowly to sudden volatility changes — a sharp spike can invalidate the channel before it adjusts.
prior_art: Keltner Channel strategy. Chester Keltner (1960). Modern version uses EMA + ATR (Linda Raschke adaptation).
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; apply to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index instead of FnO universe; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
